title: Do not close worker issues when changes are only integrated into the lead branch
body:
**Reproduced bug. Priority: P1.** Research at `6c7a6fbe`, 2026-09-06.

### Problem
“Worker finished”, “integrated into the lead”, and “landed on the final target” are different events. The current local worktree merge treats integration as final completion.

### Reproduction
1. Create a repo on main, an isolated lead branch, and worker A with a unique change.
2. Give A issueNumber 123 and call mergeWorktree with intoPath equal to the lead worktree (the path used by thread_merge).
3. Observe that main HEAD has not moved.
4. issues.completeIssue is nevertheless invoked for 123.
5. A's worktree and branch are deleted and its thread fields cleared.

The reproduction captures the actual completion call with a stub; it does not close a real GitHub issue.

### Cause
mergeWorktree unconditionally calls completeThreadIssue after mergeInto, under a comment saying the work is now on the default branch. That is false for intoPath staging and can also be false for explicit non-final stacked bases. cleanupWorktree then clears branch/worktree provenance.

### Smallest useful correction
- Classify the result as integrated or finally landed from an explicit target contract; do not infer finality from a successful squash.
- For worker-to-lead integration, retain a small durable receipt: worker ID/source SHA, target lead ID, resulting target commit and associated issue ID.
- Keep the issue open at integration. Carry included worker issue IDs to the lead's final landing so those can close once the combined change actually lands.
- Workspace cleanup may reclaim disk, but must not erase the receipt. Do not retain every node_modules tree merely for provenance.
- Failed final verification/promotion must not close included issues.
- Support nested leads without closing child issues at intermediate stages; completion must be idempotent across retries/restart.
- Do not auto-reopen historical issues by guessing from old transcripts as part of this fix.

### Acceptance
A→lead leaves A's issue open and main unchanged; lead→final target closes included issues once. A failed final landing leaves them open. Receipt survives reload and worker cleanup. Direct final merges retain their existing closure behavior. No manual UI, MCP or PR completion path can misclassify an intermediate integration as final.

Related #632 introduced automatic closure; #420 is delayed post-merge verification, not this immediate staging error. #346 covers queue execution and can use this lifecycle contract.

Sources: [thread_merge target](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/orchServer.js#L555), [unconditional closure](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/worktrees.js#L1199), [completion](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/postmerge.js#L226), [cleanup](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/worktrees.js#L706).

Evidence: `node docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-merge-evidence.mjs` exits 0. Uses a temporary real Git repo, Store and actual service/worktree functions. GitHub completion is stubbed; no live refs, remote calls or user data changed. Script is in the audit checkout; reproduction above is self-contained.

Requested disposition: separate OPEN Planboard issue, plan:todo. Research only; no app implementation.

title: Start orchestration workers from a recorded snapshot of the lead's committed work
body:
**Workflow proposal grounded in reproduced behavior. Priority: P2.** Research at `6c7a6fbe`, 2026-09-06.

### User outcome
When a lead has already integrated a worker's API or committed shared setup, its next worker sees that work without being told to reconstruct or manually cherry-pick it.

### Current behavior and reproduction
Create an isolated lead with a committed lead-only file, then call forkWorkerThread and materialize its worktree. The worker starts at main and cannot see the lead-only file. forkThread creates a new thread without copying a source ref; forkWorkerThread only flags pendingWorktree; setupWorktree chooses the worker's recorded base or repository default.

This is not an assertion that all forks should inherit dirty files. The missing behavior is an explicit source snapshot for orchestration workers, separate from where their final change will land.

### Proposed contract
- In an orchestrated integration workflow, record the lead's committed HEAD when the worker fork is requested.
- Materialize a lazily created worktree from that exact SHA, even if the lead advances before the worker starts.
- Keep start ref separate from final merge/PR target. Reusing baseBranch for both creates misleading destinations.
- Show the source branch/short SHA in worker details and in the lead's worker list.
- If lead edits are uncommitted, say that the worker inherits committed work only. Do not auto-commit, stash or silently copy those edits.
- A dependent worker launched after integration sees the new integrated snapshot. Existing parallel workers stay on their original snapshots until explicitly refreshed.
- Missing source ref must produce an actionable failure, never quietly fall back to main.
- Preserve ordinary independent thread creation and read-only/no-worktree workers.

### Acceptance
Fork from lead with committed API: worker contains it. Advance the lead between fork and lazy materialization: worker still starts from the recorded SHA. Launch a subsequent dependent worker: it sees the newer commit. Dirty lead edits are not leaked or committed. Parent identity and intended merge destination remain distinct and visible.

Builds on #187/#775 base-selection primitives but addresses orchestration fork provenance, not the manual stacked-base picker. The existing dependency list (#277) can guide when a dependent worker starts; do not create another scheduler.

Sources: [forkThread](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/services.js#L1198), [forkWorkerThread](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/services.js#L1311), [setup start](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/worktrees.js#L1544).

Evidence: `node docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-merge-evidence.mjs` exits 0. Uses a temporary real Git repo, Store and actual service/worktree functions. title: Give orchestrator leads one integration view with explicit targets and worker readiness
body:
**Usability proposal. Priority: P2; primary workflow improvement.** Research at `6c7a6fbe`, 2026-09-06.

### User outcome
Review and integrate a crew from its lead, in a visible order, then review one combined result for final landing. The user should not have to reconstruct branch state from chat messages or visit every worker's generic Merge button.

### Evidence in the current app
- The lead's AgentsPanel shows a team roster and a hidden-done toggle, not an integration list.
- thread_merge targets the caller's worktree when present. If absent, it uses the worker's base/default merge path.
- The worker's own Git-tab Merge invokes mergeWorktree without intoPath, so it can target a different branch than the lead's MCP merge.
- thread_merge returns merged/branch/into, while cleanup clears the worker's branch and path.
- Shared task dependencies, conflict forecasting, worker navigation and one-click conflict resolution already exist.
- A real two-worker test confirms conflict recovery correctly leaves the conflict inside the second worker and keeps the target HEAD intact. Preserve that behavior.

### Smallest useful view
Add an Integration section/tab on the orchestrator lead, not another global dashboard:
- Header: “Workers → [lead branch] → [final target]”, with the final route explicit: local merge or PR.
- Require an isolated lead integration worktree before preparing a multi-worker batch. A missing lead worktree must not silently make main the staging area.
- One row per worker: task, source SHA, changed files, worker checks, intended destination and state: Running / Ready for review / Conflicted / Integrated / Landed.
- Worker done means ready for review, not automatically safe to integrate.
- Ready rows stay visible after worker auto-archive; integrated rows remain identifiable from durable receipts after cleanup.
- Select workers and order them with simple controls; show existing dependency blockers. Do not silently merge every finished worker.
- Per-row Review diff, Integrate into [lead], and Resolve in worker actions use existing code paths. Generic worker-header actions must clearly name their destination and direct crew integration back to this view.
- Show combined diff and a verification result tied to the exact lead commit. Further changes invalidate that result.
- Final “Open PR” or “Merge into [target]” is one explicit human action for the reviewed combined result.

### Boundaries and acceptance
#346 already owns serialized merge execution/check gating. Use it as the execution work item rather than filing a second queue. This ticket owns the crew UI and consistent destination/readiness contract. No auto-push, new lane-port system, drag-and-drop dependency graph, or automatic batch rollback.

Test three workers: A integrates, B conflicts, C depends on B. UI records A as integrated, B as conflicted with a route to its existing resolver, and C as blocked. The lead remains navigable and no final landing occurs. After resolving B, refresh and recheck the changed candidate before resuming. UI reload preserves actual integration outcomes. Retrying an integrated row cannot duplicate its change. Missing/deleted worker paths are explained, not treated as already landed.

Pair with the staging-vs-final-completion and lead-snapshot proposals from this audit. Keep #614 user control; approving preparation of a selected batch must not imply authorization to land on main.

Sources: [team roster](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/AgentsPanel.tsx#L2672), [MCP merge](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/orchServer.js#L555), [UI merge IPC](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/ipc.js#L1346), [conflict replay](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/worktrees.js#L1263).
